history.dynasty: Eastern Chalukyas; Kulottunga I (Chola); Reddi Kingdom (inscriptional)
history.summary: Historic Vaishnava temple at Sarpavaram (~5-6 km from Kakinada) dedicated to Lord Bhavanarayana (Vishnu) with consort Rajyalakshmi. The earliest inscription is dated 1073 CE, indicating the temple existed before that; sources attribute construction to the Chalukya regime and record patronage in inscriptions of the Eastern Chalukyas, Kulottunga I and the Reddi Kingdom. It is a State Protected Monument under ASI, Andhra Pradesh, and is referenced in 15th-century Telugu works of the poet Srinatha (Kasi Khandamu, Bhimeswara Puranam). Local legend (per a place listing) links it to Sage Narada's penance of 10,000 years after experiencing Vishnu's Maya, and the Kalyana Mahostava is celebrated on Vaisakha Suddha Ekadasi. Features a 5-tiered rajagopuram, the Mukti Kasara lake, and a Paatala Bhavanarayana sub-shrine below ground level. name: Sri Bhavanarayana Swamy Temple (Sarpavaram)
town_description: Sarpavaram is a village on the outskirts of Kakinada in Kakinada district, Andhra Pradesh, on the Kakinada-Pithapuram road. It is known for the ancient Bhavanarayana Swamy temple and nearby shrines such as the Veerabhadra Swamy and Natta Rameswara temples.
